problem: Given that $n\ge 1$ is an integer, simplify $\frac{(n+1)!}{(n-1)!}.$

examples.knowledge_point: Simplifying a Variable Expression Containing a Quotient of Factorials
examples.problem: Given that $n \geq 2$ is an integer, simplify $\dfrac {n!} {(n - 2)!}.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, notice the following:

$$
n! = n \cdot (n-1) \cdot (n-2)!
$$

Then, we cancel the $(n-2)!$ that occurs in both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\eqalign{
\dfrac {n!} {(n - 2)!} 
&= \dfrac {n \cdot (n - 1) \cdot (n - 2)!} {(n - 2)!}\[5pt] 

&= \dfrac {n \cdot (n - 1) \cdot \cancel{(n - 2)!}} {\cancel{(n - 2)!}}\[5pt] 

&= n(n -1) \[5pt]
&= n^2 - n
	}
$$

feedback.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $(n-2)!$ for any $n\ge 4?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the definition of factorial, we have

$$
(n-2)!=(n-2)\cdot (n-3)\cdot (n-4)\cdot (n-5)\cdot \,⋯\,\cdot 2\cdot 1.
$$

Now, applying the factorial definition to all but the first two factors, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(n-2)! & =(n-2)\cdot (n-3)\cdot \overset{(n-4)!}{\overset{⏞}{(n-4)\cdot (n-5)\cdot \,⋯\,\cdot 2\cdot 1}} \\  & =(n-2)\cdot (n-3)\cdot (n-4)!\end{aligned}
$$
